text:
An Active Pedagogical Scenario Authoring Platform
with Collaboration and SCORM Export

Haroun Mzoughi
Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering track
University of Tunis El Manar, Faculty of Sciences of Tunis
Supervisor: Mr. RAMZI ZOUAOUI
Academic year: 2025/2026
A single workspace for an authoring lifecycle
Educational scenarios often move across separate tools.
SCORM or PDF for external LMS use
SupScenario keeps this work around one structured course document.
The project focuses on the complete authoring path.
Create structured courses with lessons, quizzes, media and decision-oriented blocks
Support co-author work, comments, review actions and controlled publishing
Export learning content as SCORM 1.2 or PDF
Learners consume exported packages through an external LMS. They do not use SupScenario directly.
Implemented scope and user boundary: presentation-facts.md; ARCHITECTURE.md §3–4.
Edit shared scenarios and exchange comments
Manage users and review submitted scenarios
Access exported SCORM packages outside the platform
An incremental implementation and validation cycle
Automated tests, build and manual demo path
The repository documents an iterative engineering process. No formal user-study result is claimed.
Methodology statement constrained to repository evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md; presentation-facts.md.
JWT-based sessions protect dashboard routes and API access
Administrators have user-management and review responsibilities
Owners, shared co-authors and administrators receive checked access
Approval states and optimistic concurrency protect review and saves
Implementation note: a production deployment requires a strong random JWT secret.
Access model: ARCHITECTURE.md §3.2, §4.2 and known issue §5; presentation-facts.md.
Lessons, quizzes, media and structured blocks in one editor
The editor keeps content in an ordered course structure rather than disconnected files.
Authors add lessons or quizzes and edit content before delivery.
Co-authors work on shared scenarios with visible feedback
Real-time gateway tracks presence and element locks
Limit: presence and locks are process-local until shared storage supports multiple backend replicas.
Screenshot: presentation-assets/collaboration-comments.png. Collaboration implementation and limitation: ARCHITECTURE.md §3.4, §4.3; presentation-facts.md.
The author reviews every proposed change
The AI service returns a version-locked change set. The author can inspect it, then apply it explicitly.
Groq tier limits can delay consecutive AI actions. Short cooldowns retry once; sustained use needs pacing.
Screenshot: presentation-assets/ai-proposal-review.png. AI proposal behavior and rate-limit limitation: ARCHITECTURE.md §3.3, §6; presentation-facts.md.
Exported packages leave the platform for LMS delivery
Package export and uploaded-package preview utility
Static export rendered through the PDF service
An external LMS hosts the learning package.
Screenshot: presentation-assets/export-settings.png. Export implementation: ARCHITECTURE.md §3.5; presentation-facts.md.
Prepared route for a short live walkthrough
Recommended live focus: open a prepared scenario, show autosave, review an AI proposal, then open export settings.
Use a disposable account and a scenario without private information.
Backend service and unit tests cover auth, users, scenarios, media/resources, AI-course behavior and SCORM services
Lifecycle transitions, access checks, AI proposal validation, media behavior and upload safety guards
Repository commands: npm run test and npm run build
No coverage percentage, performance benchmark or SCORM certification is claimed.
SupScenario connects the parts of pedagogical scenario production that otherwise remain separate.
A structured course document holds lessons, quizzes and media blocks
Shared access, comments, review actions and conflict-aware autosave
Suggestions remain proposals until an author chooses to apply them
SCORM 1.2 and PDF exports support delivery outside the platform
Contribution summary from verified implementation: ARCHITECTURE.md §3–4; presentation-facts.md.
Known constraints guide the next engineering steps
Multi-replica collaboration needs shared presence and lock storage
SCORM packages reference hosted external media, limiting fully offline use
Free or on-demand Groq limits can delay repeated AI requests
Some branching blocks have richer PDF rendering than SCORM rendering
Before staging or production use, replace the local development JWT secret with a strong random secret.
SupScenario delivers an implemented authoring workflow from structured course creation to controlled review and export.
Bundle media for offline SCORM delivery
Complete SCORM renderers for all decision block types
Share collaboration state across backend replicas
Assess direct LMS workflows or self-hosted models when justified
